title: Geometric reducedness under restriction along a separable algebraic field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k_1$ be a separable algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $A$ be a commutative $k_1$-algebra, also regarded as a $k$-algebra by restriction. Then the following are equivalent: (1) for every extension field $E/k$ the ring $A\otimes_kE$ is reduced; (2) for every extension field $E/k_1$ the ring $A\otimes_{k_1}E$ is reduced. Reduced means that the only nilpotent element is zero. These tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] carry multiplication $(a\otimes e)(b\otimes e')=ab\otimes ee'$ and unit $1\otimes1$. The zero algebra is allowed, and neither finite generation of $A$ nor finiteness of $k_1/k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, including its two-direction proof using the localization of the separable algebraic diagonal (Tag 0C2X).

proof.text: Assume condition (2), and let $E/k$ be any extension field. Because $k_1/k$ is separable algebraic, it is separably generated in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: the empty family is a transcendence basis and the extension is already separable algebraic. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] with $K=k_1$ and the reduced $k$-algebra $S=E$ gives that $k_1\otimes_kE$ is reduced, hence so is $E\otimes_k k_1$ via the swap isomorphism $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$. Regard $E\otimes_k k_1$ as a reduced $k_1$-algebra and apply [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-base-change] to $A$; it gives reducedness of $(E\otimes_k k_1)\otimes_{k_1}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] for $k\to k_1$, the $k$-algebra $E$ and the $k_1$-algebra $A$, together with the swap isomorphisms, the map $(e\otimes a_1)\otimes a\mapsto e\otimes(a_1a)$ is a ring isomorphism $(E\otimes_k k_1)\otimes_{k_1}A\cong E\otimes_kA$ with inverse $e\otimes a\mapsto(e\otimes1)\otimes a$. Thus $E\otimes_kA$ is reduced, proving condition (1).

source.place: Tag 0C2Y proof, first direction: apply 030U to $E\otimes_k k_1$ and 034N, then identify the iterated tensor product

proof.text: Assume condition (1), and let $E/k_1$ be any extension field. Via $k\subseteq k_1\subseteq E$, $E$ is an extension field of $k$, so $D:=E\otimes_kA$ is reduced by condition (1) (and the swap isomorphism). Let $R=k_1\otimes_k k_1$ act on $D$ through the ring map $\psi:R\to D$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda'\mapsto\lambda\otimes\lambda'$ (that is, $\lambda\cdot1_E\otimes\lambda'\cdot1_A$), and let $R$ act on $k_1$ through the multiplication $\mu(\lambda\otimes\lambda')=\lambda\lambda'$. We identify $E\otimes_{k_1}A\cong D\otimes_Rk_1$. Define $\alpha:E\otimes_{k_1}A\to D\otimes_Rk_1$ by $e\otimes a\mapsto(e\otimes a)\otimes1$; it is well defined because it is $k$-bilinear in $(e,a)$ and $k_1$-balanced: $(\lambda e\otimes a)\otimes1=\psi(\lambda\otimes1)(e\otimes a)\otimes1=(e\otimes a)\otimes\mu(\lambda\otimes1)=(e\otimes a)\otimes\lambda=(e\otimes a)\otimes\mu(1\otimes\lambda)=(e\otimes\lambda a)\otimes1$. Define $\beta:D\otimes_Rk_1\to E\otimes_{k_1}A$ by $(e\otimes a)\otimes c\mapsto ce\otimes a$; the map $D\times k_1\to E\otimes_{k_1}A$, $(x,c)\mapsto c\cdot\bar x$ with $\bar x$ the image of $x$ under the quotient map $E\otimes_kA\to E\otimes_{k_1}A$, is $R$-balanced since $\overline{\psi(\lambda\otimes\lambda')x}=\lambda\lambda'\bar x$ in $E\otimes_{k_1}A$. Both maps are ring homomorphisms (they respect $1$ and products of pure tensors) and are mutually inverse on generators, using $(e\otimes a)\otimes c=(ce\otimes a)\otimes1$. By [lem-trf-separable-algebraic-diagonal-localization], $\mu:R\to k_1$ is a localization of $R$ at a multiplicative subset $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] applied to $\psi:R\to D$, the map $D\to D\otimes_Rk_1$ is a localization of $D$ at $T=\psi(S)$. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced: if $(x/t)^n=x^n/t^n=0$, then $ux^n=0$ for some $u\in T$, so $(ux)^n=u^{n-1}(ux^n)=0$, hence $ux=0$ as $D$ is reduced, and $x/t=ux/(ut)=0$. Therefore $D\otimes_Rk_1\cong E\otimes_{k_1}A$ is reduced, proving condition (2).
